question: How did setting maintainer_can_modify during pull request creation change between GitHub API 2022-11-28 and 2025-06-01?
golden: In version 2025-06-01, maintainer_can_modify can be specified directly in the body during POST creation. In version 2022-11-28, it defaulted to true with no way to override it at creation time, requiring a follow-up PATCH call.

runs.answer: ANSWER: Between the GitHub REST API versions 2022‑11‑28 and 2025‑06‑01 the **`maintainer_can_modify`** field on the **`create_pull_request`** endpoint did not change in any functional way. In both versions it is an optional Boolean that, when set to `true`, gives repository maintainers permission to push to the head branch of a pull request (typically a fork). Its default value remains `false` (i.e., maintainers cannot modify the head branch unless the flag is explicitly set). The allowed values are still only `true` or `false`, and the parameter continues to be documented as “Whether maintainers can modify the pull request’s head branch.” The only differences between the two releases are minor wording updates in the documentation; the API contract for `maintainer_can_modify` is otherwise unchanged.

Explain the maintainer_can_modify parameter for this version: its type, default, allowed values, and description.

runs.answer: ANSWER: In the 2022‑11‑28 version of the GitHub REST API, the **maintainer_can_modify** flag could not be specified when creating a pull request—it was implicitly true and could only be changed later with a PATCH request. Starting with the 2025‑06‑01 version, the **maintainer_can_modify** parameter became configurable at creation time, allowing you to set it directly in the create_pull_request call.
